narrative:
The model determined that you have a 48% chance of being a bad credit risk. Because this probability is high enough for the bank to consider you too risky, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that mattered most in this decision were the status of your checking account, the amount you requested, and how long you have been employed. Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the strongest reason for the denial. Among approved applicants, only 12.6% have a negative balance, while 59% have no checking account at all. This situation strongly pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk.

Your requested loan amount of 2,406 DM worked in your favor because it is lower than the average of about 3,020 DM that approved applicants typically request. This helped pull the prediction slightly toward approval. Similarly, having been employed for 4-7 years also helped your case, as this is a reasonably stable employment duration compared with other applicants.

Unfortunately, the negative effect from your checking account status outweighed these positive factors, leading to the denial.

You should focus on improving the status of your checking account by bringing it out of the negative and ideally building a positive balance. Once that improves, reapply for a similar or smaller loan. This single change is likely to significantly improve your chances of approval. (218 words)
